name: Thiopental
summary: Thiopental (Pentothal) is a very fast, very short-acting barbiturate given into a vein to start general anesthesia, for sedation during procedures, and to quickly stop seizures in emergencies; newer medicines like propofol have largely replaced it.
description: Thiopental sodium, sold under the brand name Pentothal, is an ultra-short-acting barbiturate that boosts the calming effect of the brain chemical GABA. It is used mainly to start general anesthesia, for sedation during procedures, and to quickly control seizures in emergencies. Given into a vein, it works within seconds but lasts only a few minutes, because it moves quickly from the brain to other body tissues. Thiopental is a controlled substance (Schedule III in the U.S.) and has been largely replaced in many settings by newer medicines such as propofol.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Thiopental sodium, marketed under the brand name Pentothal, is an ultra–short-acting barbiturate that enhances the inhibitory effects of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) at the GABA-A receptor. It is used primarily for the induction of general anesthesia, procedural sedation, and rapid control of seizures in emergency situations. Its effects occur within seconds after intravenous administration but last only a few minutes due to rapid redistribution from the brain to peripheral tissues. Thiopental is a controlled substance (Schedule III in the U.S.) and has been largely replaced in many clinical settings by newer agents such as propofol.
